I am a recent graduate from the Modern Statistics and Statistical Machine Learning doctoral programme at the University of Oxford, supervised by Professor Christl Donnelly and Dr Kris V Parag.
Currently, I am working as a research consultant at Verdel Instruments, where I am developing statistical and machine learning methods to analyse 2D mass spectrometry data. I am open to other opportunities in the science start-up space. Please reach out if you have an interesting problem that might benefit from my skills.
My doctoral thesis focussed on robust statistical methods for analysing infectious disease dynamics with an emphasis on uncertainty quantification. Most recent work involved developing a theoretical/philosophical decision-theoretic framework for uncertainty quantification that is targeted to the practicalities of epidemiology, and extending existing popular methods to improve the robustness of their UQ.
Further research from my thesis combines Bayesian inference, sequential Monte Carlo methods (see also), and epidemiological modelling, with applications to standard epidemiological data, as well as survey data (see also) and wastewater-based surveillance.
During my studies, I also worked as a research assistant in the The Global Reference Group for Children Affected by Crisis, estimating orphanhood in Brazil during the COVID-19 pandemic, and held a variety of tutoring positions (departmental, college, and inter-departmental courses).
Experience prior to my DPhil includes modelling for policymakers during the COVID-19 pandemic in my home country of New Zealand (March 2020 - September 2021), a quantitative trading internship at Optiver in Sydney (November 2019 - January 2020), and a data analysis internship at a startup in Bangkok (January - February 2018).

University of Canterbury | Christchurch, New Zealand BSc (Hons) Computational and Applied Mathematics | 2019 Awarded with first class
University of Canterbury | Christchurch, New Zealand BSc Financial Engineering and Statistics | 2016 - 2018 GPA: 8.96 out of 9
I also studied statistics at National University of Singapore on an exchange programme in 2018.
